title: The Weaver's Market
story:
James perched high on the weathered mooring post at Weaver's Wharf, his eyes tracing the frantic, beautiful dance of the morning market square below. Merchants called out in overlapping rhythms, baskets overflowed with bright citrus and dried spices, and the heavy scent of roasted maize drifted over the cobblestones to mingle with the damp salt air of the canal. James had never seen so many hands moving at once, James had never heard such a loud tapestry of human voices, James had never felt so delightfully small amidst the roaring machinery of town life.

Reaching down, his fingers brushed against the smooth, cold surface of the green sea-glass Silas had gifted him, turning the glass over and over until the morning sunlight refracted through it in emerald ripples. The memory of the gentle boatman and the silent drift under Scholar's Arch felt miles away, yet the glass hummed with that same quiet stillness against the chaotic roar of the market. He pulled the brass canister of Barnaby's map closer across his chest, feeling the reassuring weight of the leather strap as a shield against the bustling crowd.

As the midday sun crested the slate roofs, a sudden commotion near a stall stacked high with woven rugs caught his attention, causing a flurry of bright fabrics to tumble into the lane. A young woman with a basket of fresh wool dropped her bundles in surprise, letting out a laugh that cut straight through the din of the square. James watched her scramble to gather the colorful spools, his curiosity outweighing his caution as he shifted his weight on the post, leaning just an inch further into the vibrant commotion.

Deciding it was time to leave his high perch and step directly into the pulsing heart of Oakhaven's trade, James slipped silently down the back of the mooring post. He adjusted his map canister, took a deep breath of the spiced air, and stepped out onto the sunlit cobblestones of the market square.
